title: Antihypertensives and the risk of serious hypoglycemia in older persons using insulin or sulfonylureas
authors: Shorr RI, Ray WA, Daugherty JR, Griffin MR
followUp: 33,107 person-years of insulin or sulfonylurea use, 1985 to 1989
population: Tennessee Medicaid enrollees aged 65 or older (mean 78 years) prescribed insulin (38%) or sulfonylureas (62%)
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central; PubMed indexes the article as supported by the US Government.
result: 598 persons had serious hypoglycaemia (hospitalisation, emergency admission or death with symptoms and blood glucose below 2.8 mmol/l). The rate was 2.01 per 100 person-years without antihypertensives; crude rates were highest with ACE inhibitors (2.47) and lowest with cardioselective beta-blockers (1.23). After adjustment for demographic characteristics and comorbidity, no antihypertensive class significantly increased or decreased the risk against non-users; against non-selective beta-blockers, each other class carried a lower but not significantly lower risk.
